8. Mr. Khan then submits that the learned lower appellate Court committed illegality in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court for declaration of title and confirmation of khas possession in respect of .92 decimals of land without assigning any sufficient and cognent reason with respect to possession trial Court upon recording evidence of P.Ws. and D.Ws and upon discussion of the evidences and other materials on record come to the conclusion that the plaintiff is in possession of the suit land. The learned Advocate, therefore, submits that the appellate Court has reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court without adverting to this finding of possession made by the trial court as such the judgment of reversal is not a proper judgment and the same cannot stand which should be set aside. 

 12. I have been taken through the judgment of both the courts below as well as other materials on record. The learned Advocate for the petitioner laid much emphasis on the point that the impugned judgment and decree of reversal of the Subordinate Judge is not a proper judgment of reversal in as much as the object of Rule 31 of Order 41 had not been appreciated. I find substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner which is well founded as will appear from a reading of the judgment of both the courts below. 

 13. The object of Rule 31 Order 41 of the C.P.C. is to see that a judge does not act callously or even mechanically. Its purpose is to put the judge on the right track and to the extent rule of procedure can do it to see that he acts judicially. It enables the High Court to judge whether the 1st appellate Court had independently considered the case with a consciousness of relevant points which arose for adjudication. It is also to afford the parties opportunity of knowing the grounds of decision to enable them to exercise the rights of an Application in revision and to enable the High Court to judge whether lower appellate Court has properly appreciated and decided the case, appellate Courts judgment reversing the judgment of the trial Court should be adequate and satisfactory. In fact, a judgment of reversal may often need a little more discussion of facts, evidence and points involved in a case so as to embody in it convincing reasons for recording the findings of the court of first instance. It should cover almost the entire grounds covered by the judgment appalled from. It must express opinion on all points on which the lower court has based its conclusion. It is however not necessary for lower appellate Court to mention each and every particular item of evidence in its judgment, provided it is clear upon reading of the Judgment itself that all relevant evidence has been substantially considered by lower appellant court. 

 14. In view of the decision of the case of Anwar Hossain and other Vs. Abul Hossain  Mollah and others reported in 44 D.L.R.(HC) page 79 and also the decision in the case of Dr. Ibrahim Hossain Vs. Mosammat Abeda Khatun and others reported in 14 B.L.D. (1994) page 346. I find that in the instant case the judgment of reversal of the appellate court does not contain adequate, satisfactory and other materials on points of possession, title and limitation and as such it suffers from illegality on those counts such as possession, title and limitation. The lower appellate Court while reversing the judgment of the trial court did not express its opinion on the points of possession, title and limitation. But in a slipshod manner reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court.
